note: Every document this package is held to or has consulted, by identity rather than by name.

authority.1: A Zilog document. What the manufacturer printed about its own part.
authority.3: Independent research. What the manufacturer did not print, worked out by measuring parts. It settles nothing on its own and is never a citation for a figure a document gives.
authority.4: A bibliography. Evidence about what exists, not about the part.
authority.why: Rung 2 is a recording taken off a real part, which is conformance/suites.json rather than a document, so nothing in this folder occupies it.

documents.title: Z80 CPU User Manual
documents.settles: The architecture, every machine cycle shape and its timing figure, the T states each documented instruction spends, what reset does, the flag register layout, the three interrupt modes and the halt state.
documents.note: The prose extracts cleanly. The large opcode map tables do not, so anything numeric was read off the rendered page image.

documents.title: Z8400/Z84C00 NMOS/CMOS Z80 CPU Central Processing Unit Product Specification
documents.settles: The two parts as products: pin functions, the speed grades each was sold in, and the electrical and AC timing characteristics. The only document naming both models this package builds.
documents.note: Every page is a scan whose only text layer is the document number in the footer, so anything taken from it was read off the rendered page image.

documents.title: The Undocumented Z80 Documented
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. It is the standard account of what Zilog left out: the two undocumented flag bits, the undocumented opcodes behind each prefix, the internal register the community calls MEMPTR, and the interrupt and refresh behaviour around them.

documents.title: Z80 Undocumented Features (in software behaviour)
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. The earlier and narrower predecessor of the document above, kept because it states some things the later one dropped.

documents.title: Undocumented Z80 Flags
documents.settles: Nothing on its own, and it is the most consequential document in this folder. It gives the flag changes an interrupted block instruction leaves behind, and it states that the Zilog, the NEC and the ST parts do not agree about the flags an SCF or CCF produces.

documents.title: Undocumented Flags, Z80Decoder wiki
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. The living version of the document above, saved as it stood.

documents.title: MEMPTR, esoteric register of the ZiLOG Z80 CPU
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. The document that worked out what the internal address register holds after each instruction, which is the register this package calls WZ.

documents.title: Z80 Microprocessor Undocumented Instructions
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. An independently compiled table of the undocumented opcodes, useful because it disagrees with Young in places and the disagreements are where the corpus is worth consulting.

documents.title: Z80 Undocumented Instructions, World of Spectrum copy
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. The hypertext form of the document above.

documents.title: Interrupt Behaviour of the Z80 CPU
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. Where an interrupt is and is not accepted, in more detail than the manual gives, including the cases around a prefix and around a repeating instruction.

documents.title: Z80 Special Reset
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. A reset behaviour the manual does not describe at all, reached by holding the line for less than the manual's minimum.

documents.title: New discovery on Z80 I/O block instructions
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. The thread in which the extra machine cycle of a repeating input or output instruction, and what it does to the flags and to the internal address register, was worked out.

documents.publisher: Manuel Sainz de Baranda y Goni
documents.title: Z80 CCF SCF Outcome Stability
documents.settles: Nothing on its own. A survey of which physical parts produce which of the several SCF and CCF flag rules, which is the evidence that a model name is not enough to pick one.

documents.publisher: Manuel Sainz de Baranda y Goni
documents.title: Z80 Technical literature
documents.settles: Nothing at all. It is a bibliography, kept because it is the list this folder was built from and because it names documents nobody has found a copy of.

documents.settles: Nothing about behaviour. Die level analysis of the NMOS part, which is the only evidence in this folder that is neither a document nor a recording, and the only place to look when a behaviour has to be explained rather than reproduced.

printedFromPage: The document was published as a web page and this is a print of it. A print is not reproducible: a different browser, a different version of the same browser, or the page having changed all give a different file. The digest therefore identifies this print rather than the page, and the fetcher will not replace one, because overwriting it with the page's markup would destroy the thing that was read.
